name: Sibal
hook: Korea's first car had a body hammered out of old oil drums by hand, wrapped around the bones of a US Army jeep.
story:
Picture Seoul in 1955. The war ended two years ago. The city is still rebuilding from rubble. But the American army has left something behind: worn-out Willys Jeeps.

Three brothers look at those jeeps and see a car. Their names are Choi Mu-seong, Choi Hae-seong and Choi Soon-seong. They run a small workshop in Euljiro.

They have no big presses. So they flatten old oil drums and beat them into body panels with hand hammers.

The engine is the strange part. The block and the drivetrain come out of the jeeps. But the brothers make their own cylinder heads, and nearly half of the engine parts end up made in Korea.

They call the car Sibal. It means beginning.

Then it wins a presidential award at an industrial fair in front of Gyeongbok Palace. Orders pour in. Taxi firms buy them. Riding in a Sibal taxi becomes something to boast about.

It stays in production until 1963. A whole car industry starts here.
description: The Sibal was South Korea's first domestically built passenger car, made from May 1955 to August 1963. Brothers Choi Mu-seong, Choi Hae-seong and Choi Soon-seong built it in Seoul on the chassis and drivetrain of surplus US military Willys Jeeps, with bodywork hammered from oil drums and Korean-made cylinder heads. A presidential award at a 1955 industrial exhibition made it popular with taxi firms. Production ended in 1963, a year after a new law opened the industry to the companies that followed.
